content: Judicial Sale of Indivisible Inheritance Assets The plaintiff, an heir by representation, sought the dissolution of the inheritance community regarding a single residential property in Rome shared with two other co-heirs holding shares of 25%, 25%, and 50%,,. This case falls under the legal framework of "scioglimento della comunione ereditaria" and the application of Art. 720 of the Civil Code,. The primary interpretative challenge involved assessing "comoda divisibilità"—determining whether the asset could be physically partitioned into autonomous portions corresponding to the heirs' respective quotas without compromising its utility,. Based on the technical evaluation of the Court-appointed expert, which concluded that the property was indivisible due to the number of participants and its structural characteristics, the Court applied the principle that in the absence of a request for full attribution by any co-heir, the asset must be sold via judicial auction to distribute the proceeds proportionally.
